subject: Post-demo: competitive evaluation — action plan & owners
content:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Zhou <alicia@stratoai.com>, Ben Strauss <ben@stratoai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: competitive evaluation — action plan & owners

Thanks again for the demo time today — great conversation. Quick recap and a proposed 72-hour action plan so we can turn the PoC conversation into a short, instrumented competitive bake-off (we'll call it "comparison trials").

Recap (from our notes):
- You (StratoAI) want a side-by-side evaluation of Redwood Inference vs Bedrock (AWS) and OpenAI/Anthropic APIs focused on: latency (p50/p95), throughput for concurrent requests, cost per 1M tokens, and instruction-following quality on your core prompt set.
- Key constraints: must be run against your sample workload (see attached sample_prompts.jsonl), include cold/hot cache measurements, and demonstrate predictable SLOs for real-time requests (<=150ms p50 target if possible).
- You asked about private deployment options for regulated workloads and whether model pinning/rollbacks are supported.

Proposed action plan (owners & timeline):
1) Smoke/setup window (Redwood infra): Fri Jul 14 — Mon Jul 16
   - Owner: Diego Fernandez (I'll provision the dedicated pool + routing rules and share credentials)
   - Deliverable: running endpoints for Redwood-hosted variant and variant with quantization/kv-cache enabled
2) Latency & throughput runs: Mon Jul 16 — Tue Jul 17
   - Owner: Rishi Malhotra (bench harness, p50/p95, concurrency sweep 1-200 qps)
   - Deliverable: CSV with latency percentiles across seq lengths (32/128/512), cold vs warm cache, token throughput curves
3) Quality eval + smoke prompts: Mon Jul 16 — Wed Jul 18
   - Owner: Marissa Cole (prepare rubrics, run automated evals, human spot checks on top 50 failure cases)
   - Deliverable: accuracy/ROUGE/BLEU-like scores and 10 prioritized failure examples
4) Cost/calc & report: Wed Jul 18
   - Owner: Diego (total tokens, cost model per 1M tokens across variants, preferred routing recommendations)

Success criteria (what will make this a win for StratoAI):
- Redwood demonstrates >= 10% latency improvement at p50 vs Bedrock on the 128-token prompt set and stable p95 within 2x of p50 under 100 qps.
- Comparable or better instruction-following score (>= baseline threshold we'll agree on) on your seed prompt set.
- Cost estimate within 20% of Bedrock for equivalent throughput (or clear tradeoffs explained).

Attachments: comp-eval-matrix.xlsx (test matrix), sample_prompts.jsonl (your prompt set), nda_draft.pdf (we discussed an NDA during contract talk)

If that plan looks good I will: provision the endpoints today, share a short test-run guide, and Rishi/Marissa will pick up their runs on Mon. Please confirm any additional metrics you'd like captured (e.g., tail-calls, mem usage, cold-starts per pod).

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---

On Sat, Jul 11, 2026 at 04:45 PM Alicia Zhou <alicia@stratoai.com> wrote:
> Thanks Diego — this reads well and captures the priorities.
> 
> Two asks from our side before you spin things up:
> 1) Please include latency at multiple sequence lengths (32/128/512) and both cold/hot cache numbers. We care a lot about p95 under real concurrency spikes.
> 2) We need cost normalized to 1M tokens with clear assumptions (vocab, avg tokens per call) and an itemized compute vs software/license split if applicable.
> 
> Also, looping in our CTO Samuel Park (cc'd) so he can coordinate infra access. Samuel — Diego will send creds and the comp-eval-matrix; please share an AWS account role if you want Bedrock runs run under our account.
> 
> Alicia
> Director, Platform Engineering | StratoAI

On Sun, Jul 12, 2026 at 09:08 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Great — thanks for the quick feedback. A few clarifications and owners from our side: 
> 
> - Marissa (me): I will own the quality evaluation. I'll prepare a 3-tier rubric (Exact match / Semantic match / Fail) and run automated scoring plus a 50-item human review sample.
> - Rishi: will own the bench harness and run the latency/throughput matrices across seq lengths and concurrency levels you requested. He'll produce CSVs and a short notebook for reproducibility.
> - Diego: infra & cost calc owner as outlined.
> 
> Proposed minimal additional metrics:
> * Cold start (first request after node spin-up) avg latency
> * Warm vs cold KV cache delta (ms)
> * Tokenization overhead and average tokens-per-invocation
> * Failure modes: 5 highest frequency error codes and last-500 logs sample
> 
> We can kick a smoke test on Wed Jul 14 PDT if that works on your side (gives Rishi & I time to prep). If you want Bedrock runs under your account, Sam please share the role. Otherwise we'll run Bedrock from Redwood account but will clearly annotate account/source.
> 
> I'll attach the rubric doc and a brief runbook after this mail (sending comp-eval-matrix now).
> 
> -Marissa
> Principal ML Ops | Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 14, 2026 at 03:34 PM Ben Strauss <ben@stratoai.com> wrote:
> Diego/Marissa — sounds good. We confirmed Wed for smoke and Mon for the full runs.
> 
> Quick note: legal asked for the NDA draft; I attached a redline in this thread. We'll sign after the smoke if everything looks ok.
> 
> Appreciate the clear owners — excited to see the numbers side-by-side.
> 
> Best,
> Ben Strauss
> Head of Product | StratoAI
